subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool expansion + hardware class upgrade (A100 → H100/L40S)
messages:
From: Arup Sengupta <arup@novametrics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@novametrics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Renewal discussion — wanting to expand Dedicated pool and consider H100s

Jonas,

We're up for renewal at the end of this quarter (current Dedicated commitment: 12 A100 GPUs). Traffic has grown 2.6x year-over-year and our throughput is the gating factor for per-customer SLAs. We want to explore: (a) expanding reserved capacity by +24 GPUs, (b) moving the new capacity to H100 or L40S for better TPU parity, and (c) adding a 99th percentile throughput guarantee for the top-tier route.

Procurement asked me to surface: the comparative cost per generated token (or per-1k-requests) between A100 → H100 and any recommended split between H100 and L40S. Also any implications for term length and pricing — they prefer multi-year terms if unit economics justify it. Can your team put together a concise proposal and perf-per-dollar analysis?

We need internal procurement review by June 25 to hit our renewal window.

Thanks,
Arup
Head of ML Ops | NovaMetrics
-----
Files: none attached

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Arup Sengupta <arup@novametrics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — wanting to expand Dedicated pool and consider H100s

Hi Arup — thanks for the clear ask. High-level response below; attaching a short proposal and an economic model for the perf-per-dollar numbers.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Expand Reserved Dedicated pool by +24 GPUs. Recommended split: 16x H100 (for latency-sensitive generation) + 8x L40S (for cost-efficient batching/embeddings).
- Term: 24 months preferred for best unit price; 12-month option also available.
- Throughput SLO: we can commit to a route-level P95 token throughput guarantee for the top-tier route; P99 throughput SLAs can be added as a paid upgrade.
- Canary & fallback: new H100 capacity rolled out canarily (10% traffic) with automated fallback to your existing A100 pool if we hit a regression.

Key perf-per-dollar takeaways (see attached model for full numbers):
- For generative workloads with avg sequence length 512 and topo of 4k tokens/min sustained, H100 delivers ~1.9–2.2x throughput vs A100 on our runtime knobs at 16-bit/amp kernels.
- L40S is ~1.2–1.4x throughput vs A100 for large-batch embedding tasks but at ~0.75x the price of H100 per-hour in our reserved pricing — good for cost-steady workloads.
- Net effective cost per 1k completions (example workload): A100 = $X.XX (baseline), H100 = ~0.9x–1.0x per-completion (due to higher throughput reducing token cost) when accounting for batch & prefix caching; L40S = 0.75x cost for batch-dominant pipelines.

Attachments: Redwood-Proposal-NovaMetrics-20260616.pdf, H100_L40S_econ-model_v2.xlsx (detailed perf runs + sensitivity to sequence length).

Next steps suggested:
1) I can host a 30-minute walkthrough of the spreadsheet and canary plan tomorrow morning PST.
2) If approved, we'll issue an updated term sheet and DocuSign for the reserved capacity and SLA addendum.

Would you like me to include a commitment-based discount tier and an optional automatic upgrade path to H100-only if utilization hits >80% for a sustained month?

— Jonas
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood-Proposal-NovaMetrics-20260616.pdf; H100_L40S_econ-model_v2.xlsx

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion — pricing and discounts (internal)

Internal notes — copying Grace for CS handoff.

Jonas: pricing guidance for ND-0429-2026 (ballpark before discounts):
- 24-month commit (24 GPUs effective on H100 class + 8 L40S): list pricing implies ~18% lower effective $/token vs rolling A100 hourly, because batching + prefix cache yields higher utilization.
- 12-month term: ~8–10% uplift vs 24-month.
- If they require hard P99 throughput, add a 12% SLA premium (applies to the dedicated pool only).

Procurement pitfalls to flag: procurement will likely ask for a termination-for-convenience clause and audit rights. We should show : (a) staging/canary results, (b) rollback playbook, and (c) a phased billing start tied to go-live (so they aren't paying until traffic cutover).

Dev: please validate the canary automation steps (blue-green vs traffic split) and confirm that fallback to the A100 pool will preserve KV cache semantics (important for tail latency).

Monica
Enterprise Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachment: internal-pricing-notes-nd0429.xlsx (internal)

From: Arup Sengupta <arup@novametrics.com>

Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — wanting to expand Dedicated pool and consider H100s

Thanks Jonas — that looks promising. A couple of clarifying questions before procurement can greenlight:
1) Can you share an explicit perf-per-dollar table for our 3 canonical workloads: real-time chat (seq len ~256, P95 latency target <300ms), nightly batch embeddings (batch sizes 1024–2048), and mixed inference (seq len 512, bursty). Put A100 / H100 / L40S side-by-side so procurement can model TCO.
2) What are the expected P95 latency (ms) and tail behavior when moving to H100 for our chat route (we run small-batch inference to keep latency low)?
3) For the commitment: we prefer a 12-month term with an auto-renew but want an option to buy down to fewer GPUs at the 12-month mark if growth stalls. How flexible are you on mid-term adjustments?

Procurement timeline: if we have the perf table and contract language by Jun 22 we can route for internal approvals.

— Arup

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Arup Sengupta <arup@novametrics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — wanting to expand Dedicated pool and consider H100s

Arup — thanks, answers and a concise perf-per-dollar snapshot below (pulled from the attached econ model). I also dropped recommended contract language for mid-term flexibility.

Perf-per-dollar snapshot (example workload numbers — see H100_L40S_econ-model_v2.xlsx for raw runs):
- Real-time chat (seq len 256, small-batch):
  • A100: P95 latency 280ms, throughput 180 reqs/sec per GPU equivalence, normalized cost per 1k reqs = $1.00
  • H100: P95 latency 220ms, throughput 360 reqs/sec (2.0x), normalized cost per 1k reqs = $0.95 (higher hourly cost offset by throughput)
  • L40S: P95 latency 330ms, throughput 220 reqs/sec, normalized cost per 1k reqs = $0.80 (good if batching is acceptable)
- Nightly batch embeddings (batch 1024–2048):
  • A100: throughput baseline = 1x, normalized cost/embeds = $1.00
  • H100: throughput = 1.7x, normalized cost/embeds = $0.88
  • L40S: throughput = 1.6x, normalized cost/embeds = $0.72 (best for large-batch embedding workloads)
- Mixed inference (seq 512, bursty):
  • A100: stable baseline, P95 ~340ms under burst
  • H100: P95 ~260ms, better headroom for burst; cost/1k completions ~0.92x
  • L40S: cost-efficient for non-latency-critical paths, ~0.78x cost but higher tail latencies

Notes: these numbers incorporate our optimizer (dynamic batching + prefix cache) and assume your current model family (open-ggml-llm-v2 equivalent) and request mix. If you have custom model forks, we can run a short spike benchmark.

Contract/mid-term flexibility suggestion (for procurement):
- Primary term: 12 months with an option to convert to a 24-month locked-in rate within the first 90 days if utilization average >65% across the committed pool for any 30-day rolling window.
- Mid-term downsizing: allow one downsizing event at month-12 limited to up to 25% of the committed GPUs, subject to a pro-rated early-exit fee equal to 10% of the remaining committed value for the downsized units.
- Billing start: phased start tied to go-live on H100 capacity or 30 days after contract signature, whichever is sooner.

Next steps:
1) I attached the perf workbook (H100_L40S_econ-model_v2.xlsx) and a short proposal PDF.
2) If that works, I'll push a term sheet that implements the mid-term clause above and a P95 throughput SLO for the named top-tier route; P99 add-on available.
3) DocuSign link will be produced once you confirm the term choice — I can issue two variants (12m w/ downsizing clause vs 24m locked).

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/sandbox/envelope/ABC12345
Redwood deal page: https://app.redwood.com/deals/ND-0429-2026

Would you like me to schedule the spreadsheet walkthrough today or Monday?

Best,
